newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian airline passengers rise 2.1 pct in Dec.
newsitem.headline: Australian airline passengers rise 2.1 pct in Dec.

text.p: Australian airlines carried more than 2.11 million passengers in December, up 2.1 percent on the number carried in November, the Transport Department said on Tuesday.
The December figures were also 1.8 percent higher than the number of passengers carried a year earlier, the department said.

Total revenue passenger kilometres (RPKs) -- the number of paying passengers multiplied by the distance they travel -- rose 4.6 percent over December 1995 to 2.38 million. The department attributed the rise to strong growth on long-distance routes.
Seat capacity also continued its strong rise, increasing 5.4 percent in December compared with a year earlier.
Load factors -- RPKs divided by the number of available seat kilometres -- averaged 72.4 percent during December, slightly less than the 73 percent recorded in December 1995.
The Cairns-Sydney route recorded the strongest growth in December, rising 12.9 percent from a year earlier, while the Brisbane-Cairns and Perth-Sydney routes both achieved growth of 12.7 percent.
Decreases were recorded for the Maroochydore-Sydney route, which fell 10.6 percent, and Launceston-Melbourne, which dropped 4.4 percent.
